description:
## What is missing

`@doc "one line"` works; `@doc """ ... """` is refused:

```
error[parse/expected-token]: compiler2 quoted front door does not yet parse Binary([...]) at item position
```

That diagnostic is a consequence of there being no heredoc syntax at all (fz-5xp.78): `@doc """` reads as `@doc ""` and leaves the following string sitting at item position on its own.

## What is left once heredocs lex

The attribute parser at `src/compiler2/frontdoor.rs:168` matches `Tok::Ident(name)` for `doc` and `moduledoc` and already takes a string token, so a heredoc that lexes to one binary token may need nothing further. This ticket is to find out, fix the attribute path if it does need something, and pin the result.

## Why it matters

Every doc string in the runtime library is one line, because one line is all the attribute has ever been handed. Elixir's docs are a summary, a paragraph on what matters, and an `## Examples` section. Matching that is the difference between a library that documents itself and one that labels itself.

## Acceptance

- `@doc """ ... """` and `@moduledoc """ ... """` carry their full text through the front door.
- A fixture proves a multi-line doc round-trips with its indentation stripped.

comments.text: Done in the commit above. No production change was required: the attribute parser already accepted a string token, so the heredoc fix in fz-5xp.78 was sufficient. Two tests pin it, one per decode path (@doc via quoted_function.rs, @moduledoc via quoted_surface.rs), asserting blank lines and example indentation survive.

title: Attach a heredoc to @doc and @moduledoc
